name: Kanban Board
tagline: A Dataverse view as a drag-and-drop board, grouped by a choice column.

limitations: Moving a card writes to the demo’s stand-in Dataverse, through the record’s setValue and save as on a form, so the move survives the next render and a change in the property panel; Reset puts the board back. The card lands the moment you drop it because the control places it optimistically and retires that override once refreshed data agrees. The movedRecordId output updates, so the value a form would react to is visible. Nothing leaves the browser.

Each lane header carries a +, because the demo’s stand-in Dataverse makes this a model-driven host. It asks navigation.openForm for the table’s quick create form, which on a form opens with that lane already chosen; there is no form behind the demo, so the event log names the form that would have opened and no card is added.

A refused move cannot be demonstrated. The stand-in Dataverse accepts every write, so the rollback never runs — on a real form a write the user has no privilege for rejects, the card returns to the lane it came from, and the failure is named above the board. That path is the reason this control catches at all, and the demo is the one place you cannot see it.

Sprint board and Narrow lanes read their lanes from the Status column’s option set, as a real view does with Lanes left empty: the labels, their order and each lane’s colour come from the options the stand-in Dataverse describes, through utils.getEntityMetadata. Lanes set by hand fills the Lanes property in instead — the route a canvas app has to take, where the option set cannot be read — and there the declared labels and colours win.

Load more works against the fixture. The board asks for its page size, and loadNextPage() adds the next page to the lanes, as on a real view, until the button goes away with every card shown. The Narrow lanes preset asks for six, so three of the nine cards wait behind Load more and the lane counts grow as they arrive — and because its lanes come from the option set, Resolved is on the board, empty, before any of its cards have loaded. The other presets ask for 50, which is all of them.
Clicking a card calls dataset.openDatasetItem(). There is no form behind the demo, so the event log names the record that would have opened. The openedRecordId output still updates.

presets.name: Sprint board
presets.description: Nine work items in the lanes the Status column's options define, each lane in its option's colour, with one item not yet triaged.

presets.name: Lanes set by hand
presets.description: The Lanes property filled in, as a canvas app has to, where the option set cannot be read: the declared labels and colours replace the option set's.

presets.name: Narrow lanes, read-only cards
presets.description: The shape for a form section rather than a full page: tighter lanes, no search box, card titles that do not open the record, and six cards at a time with Load more.
